subject: Prospect validation: Dedicated fleet certification & migration choreography

To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@canopyai.com>
Cc: Samir Iqbal <samir.iqbal@canopyai.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Prospect validation: Dedicated fleet certification & migration choreography

Hi Ellen / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, to make the hosted→dedicated move low-risk we typically run a short certification and rehearsal cadence with the following goals: validate throughput/latency with your realish traffic shape, verify prefix/KV cache behavior for your prompt patterns, and exercise rollback and fallback gates.

I attached a lightweight sizing_workbook.xlsx that we'd love you to fill with the following: 7-day peak qps, p50/p95/p99 token latencies (hosted), typical request size distribution, and any long-tail batch jobs (re-ranking, embeddings bulk jobs). That workbook will let our infra team produce a preliminary reserve plan and acceptance SLAs.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill workbook and return by Thu 9/23 EOD.
- Kickoff call with infra + solutions on Fri 9/24 (45m) to agree test windows and blackout periods.
- Staged rehearsal (staging run, 2-hour rehearsal, 24–72h canary) target week of 10/4.

I put Ben Carter and Karthik Iyer on copy — they'll lead the cutover choreography and acceptance checklist. I'm also cc'ing procurement for visibility on timelines.

Attachments: sizing_workbook.xlsx (worksheet: traffic + tokens)

Thanks —
Camila Reyes

Camila —

Thanks, this looks good. Quick notes as we start filling the workbook:
- Our 7-day peak is ~1,800 qps for inference (spiky, depends on marketing events).
- Average prompt length: 420 tokens. We have a small % (~6%) of long multi-turn sessions that rely on KV cache and are latency-sensitive (p95 target <= 120ms).
- We do nightly batch embedding jobs that spike for short windows (about 20–30 concurrent jobs).

Procurement's timeline: they're reviewing commercial terms and asked to see the migration acceptance criteria + rehearsal plan so they can align on an internal approval window (likely 2–3 weeks).

I'll have the workbook back by Thu EOD. We may also surface a couple of restricted-region requirements (EU data subset) — will flag in the sheet.

—Ellen

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Samir Iqbal <samir.iqbal@canopyai.com>, procurement@canopyai.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prospect validation: Dedicated fleet certification & migration choreography

Ellen — great, appreciate the early numbers. Based on that, here's a proposed certification and cutover choreography (high level) — sharing so procurement and your platform team can vet acceptance gates: 

1) Preflight (prep week) — deliverables: sizing workbook final, sample payload logs (first 24h representative), and proposed blackout window. Redwood deliverable: preliminary capacity plan + quantization profile recommendations.

2) Staging run (non-prod) — run hosted traffic replay into a dedicated staging fleet configured with the same model and quantization profile. Acceptance: p50/p95 within 15% of hosted baseline; no functional regressions in outputs.

3) Rehearsal (2-hour dry run) — perform a controlled 2-hour swap where a subset of production traffic is routed to dedicated fleet via routing policy (10–20% traffic canary by route). Acceptance: sustained throughput, KV cache hit-rate within expected band, no increase in error budget.

4) Canary (24–72h) — step canary to 50% then 100%. Acceptance gates at each step; documented rollback path (auto-fallback to hosted if p99 latency or error rate breaches threshold).

5) Post-migration validation (7 days) — cost and latency reconciliation, token accounting, and retro commit plan.

Timeline: if we get workbook by Thu 9/23 and kickoff Fri 9/24, we can target staging the week of 9/27 and rehearsal the week of 10/4. Procurement sign-off will determine the exact schedule; we can compress if you can commit to a 10/4 rehearsal window.

Attached: commit_plan_v2.pdf (choreography + acceptance checklist), rehearsal-checklist.md (ops runbook). Also linking the HubSpot deal for procurement reference.

Open questions for your team:
- Can you share a 24h sample of request logs with headers stripped (we only need timestamps, token counts, route ids)?
- Do you have a preferred maintenance blackout window (local nights vs. weekend)?

Ben / Karthik / Neha — any additions from an ops or infra perspective?

Thanks,
Camila
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@canopyai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Samir Iqbal <samir.iqbal@canopyai.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prospect validation: Dedicated fleet certification & migration choreography

Ellen / team —

Thanks for the numbers, that peak 1.8k qps with 420 tokens average maps to roughly ~750k tokens/sec at peak which we should size for with two considerations: KV cache working set (for your multi-turns) and the batch embedding windows. Preliminary notes:

- We recommend a fleet baseline of N+1 across the critical region with a second-region failover if EU-subset needs are flagged.
- Kernel selection: we'll use the quantization profile from our TestNet (q8_0/awq) as default but will run a fast quantization A/B in staging to validate quality and perf.
- Caching: enable prefix-level KV caching with a 48-hour TTL for session continuity; hit-rate probes during rehearsal will confirm tuning.
- Batch jobs: mirror nightly embed jobs in staging but rate-limited to prevent interference with latency SLOs; we'll size extra spare headroom for short bursts.

Acceptable rehearsal telemetry we need from your side (sample format): timestamp, route_id, request_tokens, response_tokens, p50/p95 p99 latencies, cache_hit boolean. If you can drop a scrubbed 24h sample into the Drive link noted in the HubSpot record, we'll ingest it into our load generator and produce an acceptance-grade stress profile.

We should also schedule a 30m alignment between Redwood infra and Canopy infra before staging to walk through network egress, TLS certs, and any IP allowlist work.

I'll take lead on the rehearsal runbook and will coordinate dry-run staffing (ops lead + infra + onsite SRE).

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@canopyai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Prospect validation: Dedicated fleet certification & migration choreography

Thanks — this all aligns with our expectations. A few action items from our side:

- We'll upload a scrubbed 24h sample (timestamps + token counts + route ids) to the Drive link by Thu 9/30.
- Procurement: target internal approval by 10/8; I've asked them to review the commit_plan_v2.pdf this week and confirm any contract conditions.
- Maintenance window: prefer weeknights 11pm–3am PT; weekend windows possible if absolutely necessary.
- Rehearsal: tentatively agree to a 2-hour dry run on Tue 10/5 02:00–04:00 PT; will confirm once procurement gives a nod.

On the EU data subset — that's not a hard block for the initial cutover, but we may ask for a follow-up private deployment assessment for EU-only workloads later.

I'll confirm the 10/5 rehearsal by next Tue. Thanks for pulling this plan together.

—Ellen
Head of Platform Engineering, CanopyAI
